text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Egypt moves quickly to face threats to peace process. President Mubarak tells Israel's prime minister in a message that Israel must move towards agreement with Palestinian Authority on issues on which they differ; also tells him of danger of new settlement activity and the expansion of existing settlements.
- President Mubarak leads funeral for Public Works and Water Resources Minister Abdel-Hadi Radi.
- Italian president begins visit to Egypt today. Osama el-Baz says peace process will be one of the topics up for discussion during Egyptian-Italian summit.
- Finance minister says government thinking of hiring specialised firms to manage loss-incurring companies.
- Emergency Arab League meeting on Sunday to discuss Israeli settlements.
- Italian president in Cairo today. His talks with Mubarak will cover developements in peace progress and bilateral ties.
- Palestine calls emergency meeting of Arab League.
- Agricultural banks meeting decides to reduce fertiliser prices by 20 pounds ($6) per tonne.
- As part of state campaign against corruption, 129 buildings that violate building code to be destroyed in Qatamiya.
- Egypt bids farewell to Abdel-Hadi Radi.
- Israeli buildup against Syria. Sharaa says continued occupation of the Golan Heights is unacceptable. 133 countries call on Israel to stop settlements.
- Public Enterprise minister Atef Ebeid says privatisation will continue until the end of the year 2000.
